ai.literal: Properly having investigated, further not happening by the manner, suitably punishing is king.
ai.translation: A king investigates a crime properly and punishes it proportionately, in a manner that ensures it does not happen again.
ai.modern: ஒரு குற்றத்தை முறையாக ஆராய்ந்து, அக்குற்றம் மீண்டும் நிகழாத வகையில், குற்றத்திற்கு ஏற்றவாறு தண்டிப்பதே அரசனின் கடமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the purpose and measure of royal justice. The king must first investigate a fault thoroughly. Then, he must issue a punishment that fits the crime, with the ultimate goal being deterrence so that the offense does not occur again. The emphasis is on proportionate justice rather than excessive cruelty.

ai.literal: Severely having raised, softly let strike, for a long time prosperity not departing those who desire.
ai.translation: Those who desire their prosperity to endure without departing must raise the rod of punishment severely, but strike softly.
ai.modern: தமது செல்வாக்கும் வளமும் தம்மை விட்டு நீண்ட காலம் நீங்காமல் இருக்க வேண்டும் என்று விரும்புபவர்கள், தண்டிக்கும்போது கோலைக் கடுமையாக ஓங்கி, ஆனால் மெதுவாக அடிக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises leaders on the balanced application of justice. To ensure that their prosperity and power endure, they must show strictness in their warnings but leniency in their actual punishments. The phrase 'having raised severely' (கடிது ஓச்சி) implies making a strong show of authority to deter wrongdoing. However, 'let strike softly' (மெல்ல எறிக) means the actual penalty should be mild, which prevents resentment and secures the leader's long-term success.

ai.literal: Terrifying-things having-done behaving cruel-sceptred-man if-he-is, certainly swiftly he-will-perish.
ai.translation: If a ruler is a cruel tyrant who governs by doing terrifying things, he will certainly and swiftly perish.
ai.modern: மக்களை அச்சுறுத்தும் செயல்களைச் செய்து ஆட்சி நடத்தும் கொடுங்கோலனாக ஒருவன் இருந்தால், அவன் நிச்சயமாக விரைவில் அழிந்து போவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the inevitable and rapid downfall of a tyrannical ruler. The phrase 'வெருவந்த செய்து ஒழுகும்' describes a king who habitually governs through terror and intimidation. 'வெங்கோலன்' refers to a ruler wielding a cruel sceptre, symbolizing unjust and oppressive rule. The words 'ஒருவந்தம்' (certainly) and 'ஒல்லை' (swiftly) emphasize that the destruction of such a ruler is not only guaranteed but will happen very soon.

ai.literal: "The ruler is a cruel man" saying-that which-is-spoken painful word king, lifespan having-hastened swiftly will-perish.
ai.translation: A king who draws the painful words "Our ruler is cruel" will see his lifespan rapidly shrink and will swiftly perish.
ai.modern: நம் அரசன் கொடுமையானவன் என்று மக்களால் சொல்லப்படும் துன்பமான சொற்களைப் பெறும் அரசன், தன் ஆயுள் குறைந்து விரைவில் அழிவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against ruling by terror and oppression. If a king's actions cause his people to speak the painful words 'Our ruler is cruel,' he brings about his own downfall. The word 'uṟai' has multiple meanings including dwelling, drop, and lifespan; here, lifespan or duration of rule fits best, as it 'hastens' (kaṭuki) to an end, meaning his time in power and life will swiftly perish.

ai.literal: Difficult access, harsh he-of-face's great wealth, ghost having-seen like-that it-possesses.
ai.translation: The vast wealth of a man who is hard to approach and wears a harsh expression is like a treasure guarded by a ghost.
ai.modern: காண்பதற்கு அரியவனாகவும், கடுமையான முகத்தை உடையவனாகவும் இருக்கும் ஒருவனது பெரிய செல்வம், ஒரு பேயால் பார்க்கப்பட்டு காக்கப்படும் செல்வத்தைப் போன்ற தன்மையை உடையது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the hoarded wealth of an unapproachable, cruel-faced person to a treasure watched over by a ghost. The word 'செவ்வி' here means the opportunity or access to meet someone, which is described as 'அரும்' (difficult). Because he is inaccessible and harsh ('இன்னா முகத்தான்'), his vast wealth ('பெருஞ்செல்வம்') benefits no one, just as a ghost glaring at ('கண்டு') a treasure neither uses it nor lets others approach it.

ai.literal: Harsh he-of-words, consideration he-is-without if-he-is, vast wealth prolonging without right-there will-perish.
ai.translation: If a leader speaks harsh words and lacks consideration for others, his vast wealth will perish right then and there, without lasting.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் கடுமையான சொற்களைப் பேசுபவனாகவும், இரக்கம் இல்லாதவனாகவும் இருந்தால், அவனுடைய பெரிய செல்வம் நீடிக்காமல் அப்பொழுதே அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive nature of harsh speech and a lack of empathy in a leader. The word 'கண்' (eye) here stands for consideration or graciousness towards others. If a person possesses a harsh tongue and lacks this graciousness, even the most vast and established wealth will not endure. Instead, it will be destroyed immediately without any delay.

ai.literal: Harsh words and limit-exceeded punishment, king's conquering strength wearing-away file.
ai.translation: Harsh words and excessive punishments are the file that wears away a king's conquering strength.
ai.modern: கடுமையான சொற்களும், அளவுகடந்த தண்டனையும் ஒரு அரசனது வலிமையை அழிக்கும் அரம் போன்றவையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns rulers against the use of cruelty in their administration. The phrase 'கடுமொழியும்' refers to speaking harshly to subjects, while 'கையிகந்த தண்டமும்' means punishments that exceed the limits of justice. The poet uses a striking metaphor, comparing these two cruelties to a file ('அரம்'). Just as a file slowly but surely grinds down iron, a king's harsh words and excessive punishments will gradually wear away his conquering strength ('அடுமுரண்'). The message is that tyranny ultimately destroys the tyrant's own power.

ai.literal: With the group having acted, not considering, the king, in anger having acted, if he rages, will shrink wealth.
ai.translation: If a king fails to deliberate with his council of ministers and instead lashes out in blind anger, his wealth and prosperity will shrink.
ai.modern: தன் அமைச்சர்களோடு சேர்ந்து ஆலோசிக்காமல், கோபத்திற்கு ஆளாகிச் சீறும் அரசனின் செல்வம் சுருங்கி அழியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive combination of isolation and anger in a leader. The phrase 'இனத்து ஆற்றி எண்ணாத' describes a king who fails to deliberate with his council of ministers before acting. When such an isolated ruler gives way to anger ('சினத்து ஆற்றி') and lashes out, his poor judgment drives away support. Consequently, his wealth and prosperity ('திரு') will inevitably diminish ('சிறுகும்').

ai.literal: Battle - that came - at the time - defense - who does not make - king - having become terrified - quickly - will perish.
ai.translation: A king who has not built his defenses by the time war comes will be struck with terror and perish swiftly.
ai.modern: போர் வரும் காலத்திற்கு முன்பே தனக்கான அரண்களை அமைத்துக்கொள்ளாத அரசன், போர் வந்தவுடன் அச்சமடைந்து விரைவில் அழிந்துபோவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the fatal consequences of unpreparedness. The word 'சிறை' usually means a wing, feather, or prison, but here it takes the accepted sense of a defense, fortification, or protective barrier. A king who fails to establish these defenses beforehand ('சிறை செய்யா வேந்தன்') will find himself completely exposed when war actually arrives ('செரு வந்த போழ்தில்'). Without protection, he will be overcome by panic ('வெருவந்து') and face swift destruction ('வெய்து கெடும்'). The verse emphasizes that security and alliances must be firmly in place long before danger appears.

ai.literal: Unlearned-people will-bind cruel-scepter that besides is-not to-the-earth burden.
ai.translation: A harsh ruler who binds himself to ignorant counselors is the greatest burden to the earth; there is no other.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்களைத் தன்னிடம் சேர்த்துக்கொள்ளும் கொடுங்கோல் ஆட்சி தவிர, இந்தப் பூமிக்குப் பெரும் சுமை வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet identifies the worst possible burden for the earth: a harsh ruler who surrounds himself with ignorant advisors. The word 'கல்லார்' refers to those who lack proper learning and wisdom, while 'கடுங்கோல்' signifies a cruel and unjust administration. By stating that there is no burden other than this, the poet emphasizes that political tyranny combined with foolish counsel is heavier and more destructive than any physical weight the earth must bear.
